operations.name: doc.add
operations.summary: Capture a file into the library and record a document for it
operations.long:
Capture a file into the library and record a document for it.

--file names a real file anywhere on disk; it is copied into the library
through the recoverable commit (stage, hash, immutable manifest, atomic
rename, seal - technical design §15), so the bytes end up under
library/YYYY/MM/DD because this command put them there, not because they
were pre-placed. --rendition and --attachment (repeatable) capture extra
files alongside it in the same commit, for cases like an .html original
with a .pdf rendition.

--path instead registers a file that is already inside the library at a
known relative path; it does not copy anything and cannot be combined
with --file/--rendition/--attachment.

flags.name: --attachment
flags.description: path to a supporting file to capture alongside the document; repeatable

flags.name: --body-file
flags.description: read text from this file and index it, so the document is findable by content

flags.name: --captured
flags.description: when it entered the library, YYYY-MM-DD

flags.name: --file
flags.description: path to a real file to capture into the library as the original

flags.name: --mime
flags.description: MIME type of the original (legacy --path only)

flags.name: --occurred
flags.description: when the thing it records happened, YYYY-MM-DD

flags.name: --path
flags.description: legacy: rel_path of a file already inside the library

flags.name: --rendition
flags.description: path to an additional rendition of the same document (e.g. a PDF export of an HTML original); repeatable

flags.name: --review
flags.description: when to look at it again, YYYY-MM-DD

flags.name: --sha256

operations.name: doc.reindex
operations.summary: List documents whose text is not in the search index
operations.long:
List documents that have an original file but no indexed text.

They are still findable by title and metadata, just not by content. Re-indexing needs the file's text, so this reports what to feed back through `doc index` rather than reading the library itself.

operations.name: doc.search
operations.summary: Find documents by content
operations.long:
Find documents by content.

Queries of three characters or more use the FTS5 trigram index. Shorter queries cannot form a trigram, so they fall back to a slower scan - which is how a two-character name like 杨总 is found at all. The result reports which path answered.

operations.name: library.verify
operations.summary: Reconcile the Library's journal against what is actually on disk
operations.long:
Reconciles library_packages against the filesystem, resolving every row of
the §15.2 crash-recovery matrix: an interrupted commit is validated and
completed (sealed), a staged package with no journal record is moved aside
as orphaned, a corrupt manifest or asset is quarantined, and a journal
entry whose files are simply gone is reported as an integrity error.

This never fabricates a missing file and never deletes a user's file - the
worst it does is move a package's own folder under library/_system/, which
stays fully recoverable.

operations.long:

the embedded static frontend plus a single read-only invoke endpoint.
This is not a daemon: it runs only while this command runs, and stops
on Ctrl-C or after --idle-timeout with no requests.
